sections.title: Mission · Recognize What Open-Source Technologies Do
paragraphs: Linux environments need desktop applications, server applications, programming languages, package-management systems, and software repositories. The exam wants you to recognize what common open-source technologies do.
sections.callout: WHAT DOES THIS OPEN-SOURCE TECHNOLOGY DO?

sections.title: Desktop Applications
paragraphs: Linux users can perform the same general categories of productivity work found on other operating systems.

entries.title: LibreOffice and OpenOffice.org
paragraphs: Open-source office productivity suites for word processing, spreadsheets, and presentations.
entries.recognitionCue: Documents, spreadsheets, and presentations → LibreOffice or OpenOffice.org

entries.title: Thunderbird
paragraphs: An open-source desktop email client.

entries.title: Firefox
paragraphs: An open-source web browser.

entries.title: GIMP
paragraphs: An open-source image-editing application.

table.caption: Match the desktop task to the application

sections.title: Nextcloud and ownCloud
paragraphs: Nextcloud and ownCloud provide cloud-style file synchronization, sharing, and collaboration. They fit organizations that want greater control over their file-sharing environment.
sections.callout: Self-hosted cloud file synchronization and sharing → Nextcloud or ownCloud

sections.title: Server Applications
paragraphs: Linux is heavily used as a server platform. Important server applications include web servers, databases, and file-sharing systems.
sections.callout: Identify whether the server serves web content, stores data, or shares files.

entries.title: Apache HTTPD
paragraphs: Apache HTTP Server, commonly called Apache HTTPD, is a web server.

entries.title: NGINX
paragraphs: NGINX can also function as a web server. Do not confuse it with a database.

sections.title: MariaDB and MySQL
paragraphs: MariaDB and MySQL are relational database-management systems used to store and query structured relational data.
sections.callout: MariaDB or MySQL = relational database

sections.title: Exam Trap — Web Server vs. Database
paragraphs: A website may use both: the web server handles requests while the database stores application data.

table.caption: Separate serving content from storing data

sections.title: NFS
paragraphs: NFS means Network File System. It provides network file sharing and is strongly associated with Unix and Linux environments.
sections.callout: NFS = LINUX OR UNIX NETWORK FILE SHARING

sections.title: Samba
paragraphs: Samba provides interoperability with SMB/CIFS-style file and print sharing commonly associated with Windows environments.

entries.title: Scenario
paragraphs: A Linux server must share files with Windows computers.

sections.title: Exam Trap — NFS vs. Samba

table.caption: Choose by the systems sharing files

sections.callout: NFS = LINUX NEIGHBORS · SAMBA = WINDOWS DANCE PARTNER

sections.title: Development Languages
paragraphs: Linux environments support C, Java, JavaScript, Perl, shell, Python, and PHP. You do not need to become a programmer in each one; you need recognition.
sections.callout: Recognize the common role or context for each language.

sections.title: C
paragraphs: C is a compiled programming language with deep historical importance to Unix and Linux development. Much system-level software has been written in C.
sections.callout: C = SYSTEM AND GENERAL PROGRAMMING

sections.title: Java and JavaScript

entries.title: Java
paragraphs: A general-purpose programming language designed to run through a Java runtime environment.

entries.title: JavaScript
paragraphs: A separate language strongly associated with web development and browser-based programming, although it can also run outside browsers.

sections.callout: JAVA IS NOT JAVASCRIPT

table.caption: Similar names do not make them the same language
rows: Separate language strongly associated with web scripting

sections.title: Perl
paragraphs: Perl is a scripting and programming language historically common in system administration and text processing.
sections.callout: Perl = scripting and text processing

sections.title: Shell
paragraphs: A Linux shell provides a command-line environment and can execute scripts for running commands, automating repetitive work, managing files, and administering systems.
sections.callout: Shell = command line and automation

sections.title: Python
paragraphs: Python is a general-purpose programming language widely used for automation, scripting, development, and data processing.
sections.callout: PYTHON = GENERAL-PURPOSE + AUTOMATION

sections.title: PHP
paragraphs: PHP is a programming and scripting language strongly associated with server-side web development.
sections.callout: PHP = SERVER-SIDE WEB

sections.title: Package Management
paragraphs: A package contains software prepared for installation. A package manager handles installation, removal, updates, and dependencies.
sections.callout: PACKAGE = SOFTWARE · PACKAGE MANAGER = TOOL THAT MANAGES IT

sections.title: Software Repositories
paragraphs: A repository is a source from which package-management tools obtain software packages.
sections.callout: REPOSITORY = WHERE PACKAGES COME FROM

sections.title: dpkg and apt-get
paragraphs: The Debian ecosystem uses dpkg and apt-get. dpkg works with Debian packages, while apt-get works with repositories and package management in Debian-based systems.
sections.callout: DEBIAN OR UBUNTU → DPKG AND APT-GET

sections.title: rpm and yum
paragraphs: The Red Hat ecosystem uses technologies including rpm and yum.
sections.callout: RED HAT FAMILY → RPM AND YUM

sections.title: Exam Trap — Debian vs. Red Hat Package Tools

table.caption: Match package tools to the distribution family

sections.callout: DEBIAN = DPKG/APT · RED HAT = RPM/YUM

sections.title: GSA Scenario Recognition
bullets: Self-hosted cloud files → Nextcloud or ownCloud
Web server → Apache HTTPD or NGINX
Linux or Unix file sharing → NFS
Debian package management → dpkg or apt-get
Red Hat package management → rpm or yum
sections.callout: Match the required job to the application, language, or package tool.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Apache HTTPD and NGINX → Web servers
NFS → Unix or Linux file sharing
rpm and yum → Red Hat family
